objects.definition:
enum AMFDataType
{
	AMF_NUMBER = 0x00,
	AMF_BOOLEAN,
	AMF_STRING,
	AMF_OBJECT,
	AMF_MOVIECLIP,
	AMF_NULL,
	AMF_UNDEFINED,
	AMF_REFERENCE,
	AMF_ECMA_ARRAY,
	AMF_OBJECT_END,
	AMF_STRICT_ARRAY,
	AMF_DATE,
	AMF_LONG_STRING,
	AMF_UNSUPPORTED,
	AMF_RECORDSET,
	AMF_XML_DOCUMENT,
	AMF_TYPED_OBJECT,
	AMF_AVMPLUS_OBJECT,
};
objects.description: Enumeration of AMF0 data type markers used to identify the type of a serialized AMF value. Values correspond to the AMF0 specification tags (e.g., number, boolean, string, object, null, undefined, arrays, dates, etc.).

Represents a single named AMF object member used when reading AMF object/ECMA array properties. Fields: type is the expected AMF type; name is the property name (input or output context-dependent); value points to caller-provided storage for the decoded value; size is the size/capacity for the target storage (or length for strings/arrays). Exact ownership and lifetime rules for value content are not specified in this header and depend on the reader implementation.

objects.definition:
enum AMF3DataType
{
	AMF3_UNDEFINED = 0x00,
	AMF3_NULL,
	AMF3_FALSE,
	AMF3_TRUE,
	AMF3_INTEGER,
	AMF3_DOUBLE,
	AMF3_STRING,
	AMF3_XML_DOCUMENT,
	AMF3_DATE,
	AMF3_ARRAY,
	AMF3_OBJECT,
	AMF3_XML,
	AMF3_BYTE_ARRAY,
	AMF3_VECTOR_INT,
	AMF3_VECTOR_UINT,
	AMF3_VECTOR_DOUBLE,
	AMF3_VECTOR_OBJECT,
	AMF3_DICTIONARY,
};
objects.description: Enumeration of AMF3 (Action Message Format v3) data markers used to identify the type of a serialized value in an AMF3 stream. Values map to the standard AMF3 type tags (undefined, null, booleans, integer, double, string, XML, date, array, object, byte array, vectors, dictionary). No explicit constructors/destructors; it is a plain enum used by the read/write API declared in this header.

Container for an AV1 codec configuration record derived from a Sequence Header OBU. Holds parsed flags (profile, level, tier, bit depth, chroma layout), timing fields, maximum frame dimensions, and a small buffer to store the serialized configuration record payload. Intended for creating/loading/saving AV1 configuration records and deriving codec strings.

Holds an AVS3 codec configuration record parsed from an elementary bitstream start code (00 00 01 B0) or from an Avs3DecoderConfigurationRecord. It stores bitfield metadata (version, sequence header length, library dependency indicator) and an inlined buffer for the sequence header. The sequence_header_length indicates how many bytes in sequence_header are valid. Ownership is by callers that create and pass this struct to the API; no dynamic allocations are embedded.

objects.definition: typedef struct flv_demuxer_t flv_demuxer_t;
objects.description: Opaque demuxer handle for parsing FLV tags into elementary audio/video samples. The struct is forward-declared only; its layout is hidden and managed via the create/destroy API. Details of internal fields are unknown from this header.

objects.definition: typedef int (*flv_demuxer_handler)(void* param, int codec, const void* data, size_t bytes, uint32_t pts, uint32_t dts, int flags);
objects.description: Callback function type invoked by the demuxer for each decoded elementary audio/video sample. Parameters include user param, codec id, buffer pointer/size, PTS/DTS timestamps, and flags (1 indicates video keyframe). Returns 0 on success; nonzero signals error to the demuxer.

Represents the 9-byte FLV file header plus the data offset. Contains signature "FLV", version, presence flags for audio/video, and the header data offset in bytes. Used with flv_header_read/write to parse/emit the file header. Destruction is trivial; it's a plain POD struct.

Represents an FLV tag header describing a single tag: filter flag, tag type (audio/video/script), payload size, timestamp, and stream ID. Used with flv_tag_header_read/write to parse/emit tag headers. POD; no special lifetime management.

objects.definition:
struct flv_audio_tag_header_t
{
	uint8_t codecid;	/// audio codec id: FLV_AUDIO_AAC
	uint8_t rate;		/// audio sample frequence: 0-5.5 kHz, 1-11 kHz, 2-22 kHz, 3-44 kHz
	uint8_t bits;		/// audio sample bits: 0-8 bit samples, 1-16-bit samples
	uint8_t channels;	/// audio channel count: 0-Mono sound, 1-Stereo sound
	uint8_t avpacket;	/// AAC only:FLV_SEQUENCE_HEADER/FLV_AVPACKET

	uint8_t multitrack;	/// enhanced rtmp v2, e.g. FLV_AUDIO_MULTI_TRACK_MANY_CODECS
	uint8_t channelorder; /// enhanced rtmp v2, valid on FLV_AUDIO_PACKET_TYPE_MULTICHANNEL_CONFIG
	uint32_t channelflags; /// enhanced rtmp v2, valid on FLV_AUDIO_PACKET_TYPE_MULTICHANNEL_CONFIG
	uint8_t channelmapping[8]; /// enhanced rtmp v2, valid on FLV_AUDIO_PACKET_TYPE_MULTICHANNEL_CONFIG
};
objects.description: Represents the parsed fields of an FLV audio tag header, including codec ID, sample rate, bit depth, channel count, AAC packet type, and enhanced RTMP v2 multichannel extensions (multitrack, channel order/flags/mapping). Used with flv_audio_tag_header_read/write. POD type; no special destruction.

Represents the parsed fields of an FLV video tag header, including codec ID, frame type, packet subtype, composition time offset, and a flag for enhanced RTMP usage. Used with flv_video_tag_header_read/write. POD; no special lifetime rules.

objects.definition: typedef struct flv_muxer_t flv_muxer_t;
objects.description: Opaque FLV muxer handle. The concrete struct is not defined in this header; users manage it via the provided API. Create with flv_muxer_create and destroy with flv_muxer_destroy. Used to mux various audio/video elementary streams into FLV tag payloads via a user-supplied callback.

objects.definition: typedef int (*flv_muxer_handler)(void* param, int type, const void* data, size_t bytes, uint32_t timestamp);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type invoked by the muxer when it produces an FLV Audio/Video Data payload (excluding the FLV Tag Header). The 'type' is 8 for audio and 9 for video. Return 0 on success, non-zero on error. 'param' is the user context passed at creation.

Concrete metadata structure describing audio/video stream parameters for FLV: codec IDs, bitrates, sample rate/size, channel layout flag, frame rate, duration, GOP interval, and frame dimensions. Used with flv_muxer_metadata to emit onMetaData/Script tag or equivalent.

objects.definition: typedef int (*flv_parser_handler)(void* param, int codec, const void* data, size_t bytes, uint32_t pts, uint32_t dts, int flags);
objects.description: Function pointer type for receiving parsed FLV elementary streams (audio/video). Implementations should return 0 on success; non-zero signals an error to the parser. The callback receives codec id, raw payload pointer/size, PTS/DTS, and a keyframe flag for video.

Stateful FLV stream parser context. Holds parse state, temporary buffers, current FLV header/tag substructures, and user-supplied allocation callbacks for payload storage. Subfields flv_header_t, flv_tag_header_t, flv_audio_tag_header_t, and flv_video_tag_header_t are referenced types defined elsewhere. Lifetime is managed by the caller; provide alloc/free callbacks if custom memory management is needed.

Anonymous enumeration defining FLV packet and audio packet type constants used inside FLV tag payloads. Provides numeric codes for sequence headers, raw packets, metadata, MPEG-2 TS sequences, and multitrack signaling. No named enum type is provided; values are usable as integer constants.
Anonymous enumeration of FLV video frame types used in the Video tag header to indicate keyframe/interframe and special frame categories.
Anonymous enumeration for FLV audio sampling rates encoded in the SoundRate field of FLV audio tags.
Anonymous enumeration specifying FLV audio sample bit depths used in the SoundSize field.
Anonymous enumeration specifying FLV audio channel layouts (mono or stereo) for the SoundType field.
Named enumeration describing FLV audio multitrack modes, including single track, multiple tracks, mixed codecs, and a sentinel NONE value.

No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. The API exposes only opaque void* handles returned by flv_reader_create/create2 and consumed by flv_reader_destroy/flv_reader_read. Since the underlying type is not defined here, there is no custom data type to document per the requirements.
Small I/O vector describing a contiguous memory buffer (ptr) and its byte length (len). Used by the FLV writer for scatter/gather writes.

objects.definition: typedef int (*flv_writer_onwrite)(void* param, const struct flv_vec_t* vec, int n);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a user-supplied write callback used by flv_writer_create2. The callback receives the user param, an array of n flv_vec_t buffers, and must return 0 on success or a non-zero error code.

Opaque FLV writer handle returned by flv_writer_create/flv_writer_create2 and consumed by flv_writer_input/flv_writer_input_v/flv_writer_destroy. The concrete struct is not defined in this header, so treat it as an opaque type carried via void*.
direct_api_constructors: void* flv_writer_create2(int audio, int video, flv_writer_onwrite onwrite, void* param);

objects.description: Bitfield struct representing the parsed MPEG Layer I/II/III (MP3) frame header fields per ISO/IEC 11172-3. Each member corresponds to specific header bits (version, layer, protection, bitrate index, sampling frequency, private, mode, mode extension, copyright, original, emphasis). Intended for loading from/saving to the 4-byte MP3 frame header. Note: the member name "priviate" appears to be a misspelling of "private" and remains as-is in the API. Endianness/bitfield layout is implementation-defined in C; correct serialization/deserialization should use the provided API functions.

objects.definition:
struct mpeg4_aac_t
{
	uint8_t profile; // 0-NULL, 1-AAC Main, 2-AAC LC, 2-AAC SSR, 3-AAC LTP
	uint8_t sampling_frequency_index; // 0-96000, 1-88200, 2-64000, 3-48000, 4-44100, 5-32000, 6-24000, 7-22050, 8-16000, 9-12000, 10-11025, 11-8000, 12-7350, 13/14-reserved, 15-frequency is written explictly
	uint8_t channel_configuration; // 0-AOT, 1-1channel,front-center, 2-2channels, front-left/right, 3-3channels: front center/left/right, 4-4channels: front-center/left/right, back-center, 5-5channels: front center/left/right, back-left/right, 6-6channels: front center/left/right, back left/right LFE-channel, 7-8channels

	uint32_t sampling_frequency;  // codec frequency, valid only in decode
	uint32_t extension_frequency; // play frequency(AAC-HE v1/v2 sbr/ps)
	uint8_t extension_audio_object_type; // default 0, valid on sbr/ps flag
	uint8_t extension_channel_configuration; // default: channel_configuration
	uint8_t channels; // valid only in decode
	int sbr; // sbr flag, valid only in decode
	int ps; // ps flag, valid only in decode
	uint8_t pce[64];
	int  npce; // pce bytes
};
objects.description: Container for MPEG-2/4 AAC configuration and decode-derived parameters: object profile, sampling frequency index/value, channel configuration/count, SBR/PS extension info, and raw Program Config Element bytes. Used by helper APIs in this header to parse/save ADTS, AudioSpecificConfig, and LATM/LOAS StreamMuxConfig.
MPEG-2 AAC profile enumeration (Main/LC/SSR). Useful for mapping legacy MPEG-2 profiles.

objects.definition:

objects.description: Comprehensive MPEG-4 Audio Object Type enumeration covering AAC LC/Main/SSR/LTP, SBR/PS, ER variants, layers, and other MPEG-4/MPEG-D audio tools. Values match ISO/IEC 14496-3 assignments.

objects.definition:
enum mpeg4_audio_profile
{
	MPEG4_AAC_PROFILE, // AAC LC
	MPEG4_HIGH_EFFICIENCY_AAC_PROFILE, // AAC LC, SBR (<=128 kbps)
	MPEG4_HE_AAC_V2_PROFILE, // AAC LC, SBR, PS (approx. 16 - 48 kbit/s)
	MPEG4_MAIN_AUDIO_PROFILE, // AAC Main, AAC LC, AAC SSR, AAC LTP, AAC Scalable, TwinVQ, CELP, HVXC, TTSI, Main synthesis
	MPEG4_SCALABLE_AUDIO_PROFILE, // AAC LC, AAC LTP, AAC Scalable, TwinVQ, CELP, HVXC, TTSI
	MPEG4_SPEECH_AUDIO_PROFILE, // CELP, HVXC, TTSI
	MPEG4_SYNTHETIC_AUDIO_PRIFILE, // TTSI, Main synthesis
	MPEG4_HIGH_QUALITY_AUDIO_PROFILE, // AAC LC, AAC LTP, AAC Scalable, CELP, ER AAC LC, ER AAC LTP, ER AAC Scalable, ER CELP
	MPEG4_LOW_DELAY_AUDIO_PROFILE, // CELP, HVXC, TTSI, ER AAC LD, ER CELP, ER HVXC
	MPEG4_NATURAL_AUDIO_PRIFILE, // AAC Main, AAC LC, AAC SSR, AAC LTP, AAC Scalable, TwinVQ, CELP, HVXC, TTSI, ER AAC LC, ER AAC LTP, ER AAC Scalable, ER TwinVQ, ER BSAC, ER AAC LD, ER CELP, ER HVXC, ER HILN, ER Parametric
	MPEG4_MOBILE_AUDIO_INTERNETWORKING_PROFILE, // ER AAC LC, ER AAC Scalable, ER TwinVQ, ER BSAC, ER AAC LD
	MPEG4_HD_AAC_PROFILE, // AAC LC, SLS

};
objects.description: MPEG-4 Audio Profiles enumeration describing profile groupings of tools/object types (e.g., AAC LC, HE-AAC v1/v2, Low Delay, ALS).
Enumeration of MPEG-4 AAC sampling frequency indices as used in AudioSpecificConfig/ADTS headers. Values map to standard sampling rates; 15 indicates explicit frequency elsewhere.

Top-level container for H.264/AVC configuration used in MP4/AVCC and Annex B conversions. Holds profile/level, NAL length size, counts of SPS/PPS, inline arrays of SPS/PPS entries (each with length and pointer), optional High profile extension fields (chroma format and bit depths), and a scratch buffer with an offset. The nested structs mpeg4_avc_sps_t and mpeg4_avc_pps_t are defined as members only and are not standalone types outside this struct scope.

Inner struct type for SPS entries within mpeg4_avc_t. Each entry stores the SPS length in bytes and a pointer to the SPS RBSP/bitstream. This type is scoped within mpeg4_avc_t; it is not visible as a standalone type name outside the struct scope in C, but it is a complete type used for the sps array elements.

Inner struct type for PPS entries within mpeg4_avc_t. Each entry stores the PPS length in bytes and a pointer to the PPS RBSP/bitstream. This type is scoped within mpeg4_avc_t; it is not visible as a standalone type name outside the struct scope in C, but it is a complete type used for the pps array elements.

Bitstream cursor/state for MPEG-4 style bit-level reading and writing over a caller-provided byte buffer. Holds the data pointer, total buffer size in bytes, current bit offset, and an error flag set when operations exceed bounds.

HEVC/H.265 decoder configuration container (HEVCDecoderConfigurationRecord) with parsed General/Level/profile fields and arrays of parameter-set NAL units. It holds up to 64 NALU entries with sizes and data pointers, plus an internal buffer and offset used during load/save or conversions. Details like bitfield ranges are annotated; ownership of nalu[i].data is not defined here and depends on API usage.

Container for H.266/VVC decoder configuration record (MP4/ISO BMFF). Holds length size, profile-tier-level (PTL) info, picture constraints, and arrays of parameter-set NAL units for muxing/demuxing between MP4 and Annex B. Includes an embedded native_ptl struct with detailed PTL fields and an array of NALU descriptors. Memory ownership notes: general_sub_profile_idc is an external/heap pointer managed by the API user or by loader; nalu[i].data points to parameter set payloads; data is an internal scratch/storage buffer. Exact initialization/cleanup rules are not documented here; assume zero-initialize before use and free any heap buffers you allocate for pointer fields.

OPUS identification/header structure describing an Opus stream as per RFC 7845. Holds version, channel layout, pre-skip, input sample rate, output gain, mapping family, stream and coupling counts, and per-channel mapping. Used by opus_head_save/load to serialize/parse the Identification Header payload. No explicit constructor/destructor; zero-initialization is typical. Channels value 0 is treated as 2 by opus_head_channels().

Packed structure describing a RIFF/WAVE (ACM) format header. It includes the classic WAVEFORMAT/WAVEFORMATEX fields and extends to WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE when cbSize > 0. Fields map to format tag, channel count, sample rate, average bytes per second, block alignment, bits per sample, and extensible fields (valid bits or samples, channel mask, and a 16-byte subformat GUID). Packing is 1-byte aligned as required by RIFF layouts. Construction/destruction: plain POD; no dynamic ownership. Ensure correct initialization of cbSize to indicate whether extensible fields are valid.

WebM VPx codec configuration record structure for VP8/VP9/VP10 streams. Carries static sequence-level parameters such as profile, level, bit depth, chroma subsampling, range, and color characteristics, plus an initialization data field that is specified to be unused for VP8/VP9 (size must be 0). Intended to be populated/serialized via the provided load/save helpers and from_vp8/from_vp9 constructors.

Container for FLAC STREAMINFO metadata block fields. Holds block/frame size limits, sample rate, channel count, bits per sample, total samples, and the MD5 signature of the original audio. Bitfields mirror FLAC spec encodings: channels and bits_per_sample are stored minus one; sample_rate is 20-bit value. Useful for serializing/deserializing the STREAMINFO block via provided API. Construction is by zero-initialization and field assignment; no dynamic ownership implied.

functions.name: AMFWriteNull
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteNull(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end);
functions.description: Writes an AMF0 Null value to a byte buffer and returns the next write position. Intended for incremental AMF0 serialization where ptr is the current write cursor and end points just past the buffer’s end. Details of the exact marker written are based on AMF0 and not specified here.
requirements: ptr must reference the current write position within a writable buffer.
end must point to the first byte past the end of that buffer, and ptr must be <= end.
The buffer must have enough remaining space to write an AMF0 Null value; otherwise the behavior/return value is unknown from this header.
The returned pointer (if non-null) represents the updated write position; callers should use it for subsequent writes.

functions.name: AMFWriteUndefined
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteUndefined(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end);
functions.description: Writes an AMF0 Undefined value to a byte buffer and returns the next write position. Used during AMF0 serialization.
requirements: ptr must be a valid writable position; end must be the exclusive buffer end with ptr <= end.
Sufficient space must exist to encode an AMF0 Undefined value; required size is not specified here.
Use the returned pointer as the updated write cursor for subsequent writes.

functions.name: AMFWriteObject
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteObject(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end);
functions.description: Begins an AMF0 Object by writing the AMF0 object marker to the buffer and returns the next write position. Typically followed by property name/value pairs and terminated with AMFWriteObjectEnd.
requirements: ptr must be within a writable buffer; end must be the exclusive end with ptr <= end.
Buffer must have enough space to write the AMF0 object marker.
Callers are responsible for writing object properties and the terminating object-end marker (e.g., via AMFWriteObjectEnd) after starting an object.

functions.name: AMFWriteObjectEnd
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteObjectEnd(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end);
functions.description: Writes the AMF0 object end marker to terminate an object and returns the next write position. Intended to close an object started by AMFWriteObject.
requirements: ptr must be a valid writable position within the buffer; end must be the exclusive buffer end (ptr <= end).
Buffer must have enough space for the AMF0 object end marker.
Should be called after finishing writing all object properties to properly terminate the AMF0 object.

functions.name: AMFWriteTypedObject
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteTypedObject(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end);
functions.description: Writes the AMF0 typed-object marker to the buffer, returning the next write position. In AMF0, typed objects include a class name string followed by name/value pairs and an object end; those details are not specified here.
requirements: ptr must be within a writable buffer; end must be the exclusive end with ptr <= end.
Buffer must have enough capacity for the typed object marker (and any subsequent fields the caller adds).
If a class/type name and properties are required for the typed-object, the caller must write them appropriately after the marker (not specified in this header).

functions.name: AMFWriteECMAArarry
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteECMAArarry(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end);
functions.description: Writes the AMF0 ECMA Array marker to the buffer and returns the next write position. ECMA arrays in AMF0 are associative arrays with a count and key/value pairs; details beyond writing the marker are not specified here. Note: function name appears misspelled ("Ararry").
requirements: ptr must be a valid writable position; end must be the exclusive end pointer with ptr <= end.
Buffer must have sufficient space for the ECMA Array marker (and any additional data the caller writes subsequently).
Caller should handle writing the array count, entries, and termination as required by AMF0 (not specified in this header).

functions.name: AMFWriteBoolean
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteBoolean(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end, uint8_t value);
functions.description: Writes an AMF0 Boolean value to the buffer and returns the next write position. The value parameter is treated as a boolean flag.
requirements: ptr must reference a writable buffer position; end must be the buffer’s exclusive end with ptr <= end.
Buffer must have enough space to encode an AMF0 boolean (marker plus 1 byte value; exact format not specified here).
value is interpreted as boolean; non-zero typically means true (exact accepted range unspecified).

functions.name: AMFWriteDouble
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteDouble(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end, double value);
functions.description: Writes an AMF0 Number (IEEE-754 double) to the buffer and returns the next write position.
requirements: ptr must be a valid writable position; end is the exclusive end pointer with ptr <= end.
Buffer must have sufficient space to encode an AMF0 number (marker plus 8-byte IEEE-754; exact details not specified here).

functions.name: AMFWriteString
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteString(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end, const char* string, size_t length);
functions.description: Writes an AMF0 String to the buffer and returns the next write position. The input is a pointer to a character sequence and its length in bytes; the function handles AMF0 string encoding (short vs. long string selection not specified here).
requirements: ptr must be a valid writable position; end must be the exclusive end pointer with ptr <= end.
string must be a valid pointer to at least length bytes; it need not be null-terminated.
length must correctly represent the number of bytes to write; acceptable range and short/long selection behavior are not specified here.
Buffer must have enough space for the AMF0 string marker, length prefix, and string bytes.

functions.name: AMFWriteDate
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteDate(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end, double milliseconds, int16_t timezone);
functions.description: Writes an AMF0 Date to the buffer and returns the next write position. The timestamp is given as milliseconds (likely since the epoch) and a timezone offset; exact semantics are not specified here.
requirements: ptr must be within a writable buffer; end must be the exclusive buffer end with ptr <= end.
Buffer must have enough space to encode an AMF0 date (marker, 8-byte milliseconds, and 2-byte timezone; exact details not specified here).
milliseconds and timezone ranges/units are not specified in this header; callers must supply meaningful values for their use case.

functions.name: AMFWriteNamed
functions.signature: uint8_t* AMFWriteNamed(uint8_t* ptr, const uint8_t* end, const char* name, size_t length);
functions.description: Writes an AMF0 object property name (string) to the buffer and returns the next write position. Typically used before writing a property value when serializing objects or ECMA arrays.
requirements: ptr must be a valid writable position; end must be the exclusive buffer end with ptr <= end.
name must point to at least length bytes; it need not be null-terminated.
length must correctly represent the number of bytes in the name.

functions.description: Parses an FLV video tag header from buf and fills video with codec, frame type, packet type, composition time (CTS), and whether enhanced RTMP is used. Returns the header length in bytes on success or a negative value on error. Use after identifying a video tag to interpret payload timing and codec.
requirements: video must be a valid, writable pointer to struct flv_video_tag_header_t
buf must be a valid, readable pointer to the start of an FLV video tag header
len must be sufficient for the video tag header (exact minimum not stated)

Field meanings: codecid is video codec ID (e.g., FLV_VIDEO_H264); keyframe is frame type (1=key, 2=inter); avpacket for H.264/H.265/AV1 indicates FLV_SEQUENCE_HEADER/FLV_AVPACKET/FLV_END_OF_SEQUENCE; cts is composition-time offset (PTS - DTS) for AVC/HEVC/AV1
Caller must handle return value: >=0 header length; <0 indicates error and video contents are unspecified

Caller must check return value: >=0 bytes written; <0 indicates failure

Use this when tags are already delineated: pass the tag type, a buffer containing the tag payload (AudioTagHeader/VideoTagHeader followed by A/V data), its length, and the tag timestamp (milliseconds, DTS relative to the first tag). The handler will receive decoded elementary stream frames (e.g., AAC frame, H.264/MP4 stream, MP3 raw). Returns 0 on success, non‑zero on error.
requirements: type must indicate the tag kind: 8 for audio, 9 for video, or 18 for script.
data must point to a valid buffer containing the FLV tag payload; for audio/video this includes the AudioTagHeader/VideoTagHeader followed by the corresponding A/V data.
bytes must equal the number of bytes available at data; must be sufficient to contain the stated headers and payload.
timestamp is a 32-bit millisecond value relative to the first tag (DTS).
handler must be a valid function matching flv_parser_handler; it will be invoked with codec, data pointer, size, pts/dts, and flags (flags==1 indicates a video keyframe).
param is an opaque user pointer passed through to handler.
Function returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

Use this for streaming input: supply successive chunks of FLV data; the function consumes bytes according to internal state and emits frames via the callback. Returns 0 on success, non‑zero on error.

data must point to a buffer of at least bytes bytes containing FLV stream data; may be called repeatedly with subsequent chunks.
bytes specifies the number of bytes available at data; can be zero to indicate no input (behavior not documented).

Function returns 0 on success; non-zero indicates an error.

Return semantics on failure are not documented here (likely NULL on error).

file must remain a valid, null-terminated string for the duration of this call.
The returned handle (if non-NULL) must be passed to flv_reader_read and eventually to flv_reader_destroy.
Do not use the handle after it has been passed to flv_reader_destroy.
Error/NULL return behavior is not explicitly documented; caller should check for a null/invalid handle before use (assumed pattern).

Returns an opaque reader handle used with flv_reader_read and flv_reader_destroy. The exact contract of the read callback’s return value is not documented here; by naming convention it likely mirrors POSIX read: return number of bytes read, 0 for EOF, and negative on error.
requirements: read must be a valid function pointer with signature int(void* param, void* buf, int len).

read must write up to len bytes into buf and return an integer indicating how many bytes were provided; precise semantics (EOF/error) are not documented in this header and should follow the library’s implementation expectations (likely: >=0 bytes read, 0=EOF, <0=error).
buf provided to the callback will be a valid writable buffer of at least len bytes for the duration of the call.
param is an opaque user pointer passed through to the callback; it must remain valid for all invocations until flv_reader_destroy.
The returned handle (if non-NULL) must be passed to flv_reader_read and eventually to flv_reader_destroy.
Do not use the handle after it has been passed to flv_reader_destroy.
Error/NULL return behavior is not explicitly documented; caller should check for a null/invalid handle before use (assumed pattern).

requirements: flv must be a handle previously returned by flv_reader_create or flv_reader_create2.

functions.description: Read the next FLV tag into the caller-supplied buffer and return its metadata. On success returns 1; on end of input returns 0; any other return indicates an error. Outputs: tagtype (8=audio, 9=video, 18=script data), timestamp (FLV timestamp), taglen (tag length; 0-length tags are valid but should be discarded by the caller). The FLV tag bytes are written to buffer, up to the provided capacity.
requirements: flv must be a valid reader handle created by flv_reader_create or flv_reader_create2 and not yet destroyed.
tagtype must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the tag type.
timestamp must be a non-NULL pointer to uint32_t to receive the FLV timestamp.
taglen must be a non-NULL pointer to size_t to receive the tag length.
buffer must be a valid writable memory region of at least bytes bytes for the duration of the call.
bytes specifies the size of buffer in bytes and should be large enough to hold the incoming FLV tag; if smaller than the tag, behavior is not documented in this header.
Return value handling: 1 means a packet was read and outputs are valid; 0 means EOF; any other value indicates an error and outputs may be undefined.
Caller should silently discard tags where the returned taglen is 0, per comment note.

returns 0 on success, other values indicate error and should be handled by the caller (documented)

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for AMF0 short string bytes (the raw character payload only).
# The fuzz stubs will limit lengths to <=256 for values and <=128 for names.
# We return a single buffer that the harness will use for FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FILENAME.
# To maximize coverage across AMF writers, we compose a corpus of interesting strings
# separated by NULs so the fuzzer can slice or choose among them. Each substring is
# valid UTF-8 or intentionally binary but acceptable for AMF0 strings.

MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 4096

ASCII_VISIBLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "


def _be_utf8_sequences() -> List[bytes]:
    # A mix of UTF-8 edge cases
    samples = [
        "".encode("utf-8"),  # empty
        "hello".encode("utf-8"),
        ("a" * 1).encode("utf-8"),
        ("b" * 31).encode("utf-8"),
        ("c" * 127).encode("utf-8"),
        ("𝄞" * 8).encode("utf-8"),  # 4-byte codepoint
        "café".encode("utf-8"),
        "日本語".encode("utf-8"),
        "emoji: 😀😇😈".encode("utf-8"),
        "null\x00byte".encode("latin1"),
        # Boundary lengths around the stub limits
        bytes([0x41]) * 2,
        bytes([0x41]) * 3,
        bytes([0x41]) * 7,
        bytes([0x41]) * 15,
        bytes([0x41]) * 31,
        bytes([0x41]) * 63,
        bytes([0x41]) * 95,
        bytes([0x41]) * 127,
        bytes([0x41]) * 128,  # name upper bound in stub
        bytes([0x42]) * 255,
        bytes([0x42]) * 256,  # value upper bound in stub
    ]
    return samples


def _binary_patterns() -> List[bytes]:
    # Interesting binary patterns valid for AMF0 String payloads
    pats = []
    pats.append(bytes(range(0, 128)))  # 0..127 ASCII control+basic
    pats.append(bytes([0x00] * 64))    # all zeros
    pats.append(bytes([0xFF] * 64))    # all 0xFF
    # Repeating marker-like bytes to test adjacent parsing
    pats.append(bytes([0x02]) * 32)    # AMF0 string marker value repeated inside payload
    pats.append(bytes([0x01]) * 32)    # boolean marker value repeated
    # Mixed alternating patterns
    pats.append(bytes([0x00, 0xFF]) * 32)
    pats.append(bytes([0x55, 0xAA]) * 32)
    return pats


def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_VISIBLE) for _ in range(n)).encode('latin1')


def _random_utf8(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Build random unicode then encode; ensure <= n bytes by truncation on bytes
    s = []
    while len(''.join(s).encode('utf-8')) < n:
        # mix BMP and supplementary planes
        cp = rng.choice([
            rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E),
            rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x07FF),
            rng.randint(0x0800, 0xFFFF),
            rng.randint(0x10000, 0x10FFFF),
        ])
        # avoid surrogate halves
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            continue
        s.append(chr(cp))
        if len(s) > n:  # guard
            break
    b = ''.join(s).encode('utf-8')
    return b[:n]


def _make_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus: List[bytes] = []

    # Deterministic interesting cases
    corpus.extend(_be_utf8_sequences())
    corpus.extend(_binary_patterns())

    # Add random sized ASCII and UTF-8 up to the stub limits
    for _ in range(12):
        corpus.append(_random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 256)))
    for _ in range(12):
        corpus.append(_random_utf8(rng, rng.randint(1, 256)))

    # Add a few name-like and value-like pairs to encourage NamedString usage
    keys = [
        b"onMetaData",
        b"duration",
        b"width",
        b"height",
        b"videocodecid",
        b"audiocodecid",
        b"title",
        b"author",
        b"language",
    ]
    values = [
        b"true",
        b"false",
        b"0",
        b"1",
        b"23.976",
        b"29.97",
        b"44100",
        b"48000",
        b"H.264",
        b"HEVC",
        b"AV1",
        b"AAC",
        b"Opus",
    ]
    corpus.extend(keys)
    corpus.extend(values)

    # Clip items to max per AMF0 short-string path (<= 65535), but stubs use <=256/128
    clipped = []
    for s in corpus:
        if len(s) > 256:
            clipped.append(s[:256])
        else:
            clipped.append(s)

    # Shuffle to mix
    rng.shuffle(clipped)
    return clipped


def _pack_corpus(items: List[bytes], rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate items separated by zero bytes; include some length-prefixed regions
    # even though the stub only needs raw payloads, having multiple chunks lets the
    # harness pull different slices.
    out = bytearray()
    for b in items:
        if len(out) + len(b) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
            break
        out += b
        out += b"\x00"  # separator

    # Optionally append a small self-describing segment: [len_be16][raw]
    # This remains valid as raw string bytes since callers use only the bytes
    # themselves; but some consumers may pick a substring starting after the length.
    if len(out) + 2 + 64 <= MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
        seg = _random_utf8(rng, rng.randint(8, 64))
        out += struct.pack(">H", len(seg)) + seg

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(b"\x00")
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    items = _make_corpus(rng)
    # Choose a random subset size
    k = rng.randint(min(4, len(items)), min(24, len(items)))
    subset = rng.sample(items, k)
    return _pack_corpus(subset, rng)

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: AMF0 property name (and used in named value writers)
# On-wire encoding for an AMF0 property name is:
#   uint16_be name_length; name_bytes[name_length]
# For the fuzzer stubs:
# - AMFWriteNamed(name,len) only needs a valid name byte sequence of length len (no marker)
# - AMFWriteNamedString/Double/Boolean: they compute their own space and call the writer; our FUZZ_PARAM_STR
#   will supply interesting name and value strings. The buffers are sized using those lengths.
# This generator returns a bytes buffer that will be used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME machinery.
# We therefore aim to provide a sequence of interesting UTF-8/ASCII-friendly strings concatenated, so that
# successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls slice from this buffer to produce names/values with diverse content.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a small corpus of candidate strings covering edge cases and typical cases:
#   * empty string, 1-char, max short names near 128/256 boundaries
#   * ASCII, UTF-8 multibyte, control chars, high-bit bytes
#   * Names often used in FLV/AMF metadata (onMetaData keys)
# - Concatenate them separated by NUL to encourage distinct FUZZ_PARAM_STR splits.
# - Total size kept <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Note: We don’t add AMF markers; only raw bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR to consume.

_DEF_META_KEYS = [
    "duration", "width", "height", "videocodecid", "audiosamplerate",
    "audiosamplesize", "stereo", "audiocodecid", "framerate", "filesize",
    "encoder", "creationDate", "server", "onMetaData"
]

_UTF8_EXAMPLES = [
    "naïve",            # composed
    "café",             # accented
    "ключ",             # Cyrillic
    "漢字",              # CJK
    "😀",               # emoji (4-byte UTF-8)
    "¡Olé!",            # inverted exclaim + accent
    "Δοκιμή",           # Greek
]

_CTRL_SEQS = [
    "\tname\n", " name ", "name\x00with\x00null", "\x7Fdel", "\x01\x02bin"
]

def _random_ascii(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Visible ASCII plus a few punctuation
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:." 
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _random_utf8(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Mix ascii with occasional multibyte code points
    s: List[str] = []
    while len(''.join(s).encode('utf-8')) < length:
        pick = rng.random()
        if pick < 0.75:
            s.append(_random_ascii(rng, 1))
        elif pick < 0.9:
            s.append(rng.choice(_UTF8_EXAMPLES))
        else:
            # random BMP code point avoiding surrogates
            cp = rng.randint(0x20, 0xFFFD)
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                cp = 0x20
            s.append(chr(cp))
    # Trim to target byte length approximately (safe to be longer; FUZZ side will cap names)
    out = ''.join(s)
    # Soft trim to desired byte length window
    b = out.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > length:
        # try to truncate at a char boundary by decoding after slicing down
        cut = length
        while cut > 0:
            try:
                return b[:cut].decode('utf-8', 'strict')
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                cut -= 1
        return ''
    return out

def _build_corpus(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # Fixed interesting names
    fixed = [
        "", "a", "A", "_", "0",
        "x" * 3, "long_name", "NAME", "camelCase", "snake_case",
    ]
    fixed += _DEF_META_KEYS
    fixed += _UTF8_EXAMPLES
    fixed += _CTRL_SEQS

    # Boundary-length names around 1, 2, 127, 128, 255, 256 (short strings are capped <=256 in stubs)
    for L in [1, 2, 15, 31, 63, 127, 128, 200, 255, 256]:
        s = _random_utf8(rng, L)
        fixed.append(s)

    # Some numeric-looking strings for values
    fixed += [
        "0", "1", "-1", "3.14159", "2.99792458e8", "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity"
    ]

    # Random batch
    for _ in range(40):
        L = rng.randint(0, 256)
        s = _random_utf8(rng, L)
        fixed.append(s)

    # Assemble with NUL separators and occasional length-prefixed blobs to exercise consumers
    for s in fixed:
        enc = s.encode('utf-8')
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            # Prepend a 16-bit length hint then bytes; some consumers may read raw bytes
            prefix = struct.pack('>H', len(enc) if len(enc) <= 0xFFFF else 0)
            piece = prefix + enc
        else:
            piece = enc
        chunks.append(piece)
        chunks.append(b"\x00")  # separator
        if sum(len(c) for c in chunks) >= budget:
            break

    data = b"".join(chunks)[:budget]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Keep under 4096 bytes total
    budget = rng.randint(512, 2048)
    buf = _build_corpus(rng, budget)
    # Ensure non-empty
    if not buf:
        buf = b"\x00"
    return buf

import random
import struct
import string

# Target: AMFReadString fuzzer stub expects a full AMF0 short or long string value
# Layouts considered by the stub:
# - Short string: [0x02][u16_be length][payload]
# - Long string:  [0x0C][u32_be length][payload]
# The stub decides short/long randomly and caps short strings to <= 200 bytes.
# We generate valid frames covering both cases with interesting payloads.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _interesting_strings(rng: random.Random):
    # A set of payload candidates to exercise different behaviors
    samples = [
        "",  # empty
        "a",
        "hello",
        "A" * 200,  # short-string boundary used by stub
        "B" * 201,  # will be used only for long string (short is capped in stub)
        "\x00" * 16,  # contains NULs

# AMF0 markers
AMF0_NUMBER = 0x00
AMF0_BOOLEAN = 0x01
AMF0_STRING = 0x02
AMF0_OBJECT = 0x03
AMF0_OBJECT_END = b"\x00\x00\x09"

# Build AMF0 short string (<= 65535)
def _amf0_string(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(s) > 0xFFFF:
        s = s[:0xFFFF]
    return bytes([AMF0_STRING]) + struct.pack(">H", len(s)) + s

# Build AMF0 boolean
def _amf0_boolean(v: bool) -> bytes:
    return bytes([AMF0_BOOLEAN, 1 if v else 0])

# Build AMF0 number (IEEE-754 double, big-endian per AMF0)
def _amf0_number(d: float) -> bytes:
    # Use big-endian network order for AMF0 doubles
    return bytes([AMF0_NUMBER]) + struct.pack(">d", float(d))

# Property name encoding: 2-byte big-endian length + bytes
def _prop_name(name: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", len(name)) + name

# Make a safe ASCII name [a-z0-9], length 1..16
def _gen_name(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    nlen = rng.randint(1, 16)
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(nlen):
        if i % 2:
            out.append(ord('a') + rng.randrange(26))
        else:
            out.append(ord('0') + rng.randrange(10))
    return bytes(out)

# Generate a reasonable UTF-8 payload with common ASCII and some extended bytes
def _gen_string_bytes(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> bytes:
    # Keep within 64 to match stub expectations and avoid long buffers
    ln = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    # Mix of ASCII letters/digits and spaces; occasionally include simple UTF-8 2-byte sequences
    b = bytearray()
    while len(b) < ln:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.85:
            b.append(rng.choice(list(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-./")))
        else:
            # simple 2-byte UTF-8 for U+00A0..U+07FF
            cp = rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x07FF)
            if cp < 0x80:
                b.append(cp)
            elif cp < 0x800:
                b.append(0xC0 | (cp >> 6))
                b.append(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F))
            else:
                b.append(cp & 0x7F)
    return bytes(b[:ln])

# Generate diverse doubles that are still valid IEEE-754
def _gen_double(rng: random.Random) -> float:
    kinds = [
        lambda: 0.0,
        lambda: -0.0,
        lambda: 1.0,
        lambda: -1.0,
        lambda: float('inf'),
        lambda: float('-inf'),
        # Avoid NaN since some parsers may reject or canonicalize it; still occasionally include
        lambda: float('nan'),
        lambda: rng.uniform(-1e9, 1e9),
        lambda: 2.0 ** rng.randint(-20, 20),
        lambda: math.pi,
        lambda: math.e,
    ]
    v = rng.choice(kinds)()
    return v

# Build an AMF0 object with one property and a matching value type
# Layout: 0x03, name (u16+bytes), value, 0x00 0x00 0x09

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Pick which value type: 0-number, 1-string, 2-boolean
    which = rng.randrange(3)

    name = _gen_name(rng)

    body = bytearray()
    body.append(AMF0_OBJECT)
    body += _prop_name(name)

    if which == 0:
        d = _gen_double(rng)
        # Some consumers dislike NaN; clamp probability: if NaN chosen, occasionally replace
        if isinstance(d, float) and math.isnan(d) and rng.random() < 0.7:
            d = 0.0
        body += _amf0_number(d)
    elif which == 1:
        s = _gen_string_bytes(rng, 64)
        body += _amf0_string(s)
    else:
        b = bool(rng.randrange(2))
        body += _amf0_boolean(b)

    body += AMF0_OBJECT_END

    # Ensure size limit
    return bytes(body[:4096])

# Data type: AMF3 null marker buffer

_MAX_SIZE = 64  # fuzzer stub caps at 64
_MIN_SIZE = 1

_DEF_PADDING_PATTERNS: List[bytes] = [
    # Use only non-empty patterns here; empty handled separately to avoid zero-division
    b"\x00",
    b"\x00\x00\x00",
    b"\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00",
    b"\xff" * 8,
    b"\xaa\x55" * 8,
    b"AMF3NULL",
    bytes(range(1, 32)),  # increasing small integers (avoid 0 for variety)
]


def _rand_padding(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    if target_len <= 1:
        return b""
    need = target_len - 1
    # Occasionally pick from predefined patterns trimmed/expanded to size
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pat = rng.choice(_DEF_PADDING_PATTERNS)
        plen = len(pat)
        if plen == 0:
            # Fallback to random bytes if somehow empty (shouldn't happen now)
            return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(need))
        if plen >= need:
            return pat[:need]
        else:
            reps = (need + plen - 1) // plen
            return (pat * reps)[:need]
    # Otherwise, generate random padding with some biased bytes
    bias = [0x00, 0x01, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF]
    out = bytearray(need)
    for i in range(need):
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            out[i] = rng.choice(bias)
        else:
            out[i] = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a size with a bias toward small and a few larger cases
    choices = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 48, 64]
    # Weight toward smaller sizes
    weights = [30, 20, 15, 12, 10, 7, 4, 2]
    size = rng.choices(choices, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    size = max(_MIN_SIZE, min(_MAX_SIZE, size))

    # Build buffer: first byte is AMF3 null marker 0x01
    padding = _rand_padding(rng, size)
    buf = bytearray(1 + len(padding))
    buf[0] = 0x01
    if padding:
        buf[1:] = padding
    return bytes(buf)

# The fuzzer stub builds the final buffer as: [0x05] + first 8 bytes from FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
# Therefore, our generator should return exactly those 8 bytes (the marker is added by the stub),
# and they should represent interesting but valid IEEE-754 doubles in big-endian order.

_INTERESTING_DOUBLES = [
    0.0,
    -0.0,
    1.0,
    -1.0,
    2.0,
    0.5,
    1.5,
    3.141592653589793,
    -3.141592653589793,
    float('inf'),
    float('-inf'),
    # A quiet NaN with a deterministic payload
    struct.unpack('>d', bytes.fromhex('7ff8000000000001'))[0],
    # Subnormal smallest positive
    struct.unpack('>d', b"\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01")[0],
    # Largest finite
    struct.unpack('>d', bytes.fromhex('7fefffffffffffff'))[0],
    # Tiny negative subnormal
    struct.unpack('>d', b"\x80\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01")[0],
]

# Additional ranges to explore exponents and mantissas
_DEF_RANGES = [
    # (min_exp, max_exp) in unbiased exponent terms for IEEE754 double
    (-1022, -900),   # subnormal/very small normals vicinity
    (-100, 100),     # mid-range
    (900, 1023),     # very large normals vicinity
]


def _random_double(rnd: random.Random) -> float:
    # Mix between interesting constants and random constructions
    choice = rnd.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        return rnd.choice(_INTERESTING_DOUBLES)

    # Construct random finite/NaN/Inf with some bias
    kind = rnd.random()
    if kind < 0.1:
        # Infinity
        return math.inf if rnd.random() < 0.5 else -math.inf
    if kind < 0.2:
        # NaN with random payload (quiet NaN)
        payload = rnd.getrandbits(51)
        sign = rnd.getrandbits(1)
        bits = (sign << 63) | (0x7ff << 52) | (1 << 51) | payload
        return struct.unpack('>d', bits.to_bytes(8, 'big'))[0]

    # Finite
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        # Subnormal construction
        sign = rnd.getrandbits(1)
        mant = rnd.getrandbits(52)
        exp = 0  # subnormal
        bits = (sign << 63) | (exp << 52) | (mant & ((1 << 52) - 1))
        return struct.unpack('>d', bits.to_bytes(8, 'big'))[0]

    # Normal finite with controlled exponent
    sign = rnd.getrandbits(1)
    er = rnd.choice(_DEF_RANGES)
    unbiased_exp = rnd.randint(er[0], er[1])
    biased = unbiased_exp + 1023
    if biased <= 0:
        biased = 1
    if biased >= 0x7ff:
        biased = 0x7fe
    mant = rnd.getrandbits(52)
    bits = (sign << 63) | (biased << 52) | mant
    return struct.unpack('>d', bits.to_bytes(8, 'big'))[0]

    # Ensure big-endian IEEE-754
    return struct.pack('>d', value)

    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how to craft the 8 payload bytes the stub will copy after the 0x05 marker
    # We aim to sometimes provide structured doubles and sometimes arbitrary bytes that
    # still decode as doubles (all 8-byte patterns decode to some double value).

    mode = rnd.random()
    if mode < 0.85:

        val = _random_double(rnd)

        payload = rnd.randbytes(8) if hasattr(rnd, 'randbytes') else bytes([rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(8)])

    # Limit to 4096 bytes: we only return the 8-byte payload the stub will consume.
    return payload

# This generator builds a minimal, but valid AV1 Low-Overhead bitstream sample
# containing a single Sequence Header OBU wrapped in a Length-Delimited OBU
# (temporal_delimiter optional). It aims to satisfy aom_av1_codec_configuration_record_init.
#
# AV1 Low Overhead OBU framing (per spec / ISOBMFF):
#   [leb128 obu_length][obu_header + obu_payload]
# OBU header:
#   bits: forbidden(1=0), obu_type(4), obu_extension_flag(1=0), obu_has_size_field(1=1), obu_reserved_1bit(1=0)
#   followed by leb128 obu_payload_length (inside the OBU block)
# For Sequence Header OBU, payload is sequence_header_obu() with required fields.
# This payload is non-trivial, but we can produce a conservative configuration:
#   - seq_profile=0, still_picture=0, reduced_still_picture_header=0
#   - timing_info absent, decoder_model_info absent, initial_display_delay absent
#   - operating_points_cnt_minus_1=0, default operating point flags
#   - frame_width_bits/frame_height_bits with reasonable values; max_frame_width/height set
#   - enable_* tool flags mostly 0 to simplify
#   - color config: 8-bit 4:2:0 limited, BT.709 primaries/transfer/matrix defaults
#   - film_grain_params_present=0
# This should parse in many implementations. Values randomized within valid ranges.

# LEB128 helpers (unsigned)
def leb128_encode_u(value: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        b = value & 0x7F
        value >>= 7
        if value:
            out.append(0x80 | b)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

class BitWriter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.buf = bytearray()
        self.acc = 0
        self.nbits = 0
    def write_bit(self, v: int):
        self.acc = (self.acc << 1) | (1 if v else 0)
        self.nbits += 1
        if self.nbits == 8:
            self.buf.append(self.acc & 0xFF)
            self.acc = 0
            self.nbits = 0
    def write_bits(self, v: int, n: int):
        for i in range(n-1, -1, -1):
            self.write_bit((v >> i) & 1)
    def byte_align(self):
        if self.nbits:
            self.buf.append((self.acc << (8 - self.nbits)) & 0xFF)
            self.acc = 0
            self.nbits = 0
    def get(self) -> bytes:
        self.byte_align()
        return bytes(self.buf)

# Color config per spec (simplified path when high_bitdepth=0)

    if profile == 2:

        bw.write_bits(1, 8)
        bw.write_bits(1, 8)

    # Nothing more in color_config for 8-bit profile 0 minimal path.

    # seq_profile(3)

    bw.write_bits(profile, 3)

    still_picture = 0
    bw.write_bit(still_picture)
    # reduced_still_picture_header(1)
    reduced_still = 0
    bw.write_bit(reduced_still)

    bw.write_bit(0)
    # decoder_model_info_present_flag(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # initial_display_delay_present_flag(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)

    # operating_points_cnt_minus_1(5)
    bw.write_bits(0, 5)
    # For operating point 0
    # operating_point_idc(12)
    bw.write_bits(0, 12)
    # seq_level_idx[op](5) choose a common level like 31 (level 3.1) or 20 (2.0)
    level = rng.choice([20, 21, 30, 31, 40])
    bw.write_bits(level, 5)
    # seq_tier[op] present if level>7; ours is >7 so include 1 bit
    tier = 0
    bw.write_bit(tier)
    # decoder_model_present_for_this_op(1) since decoder_model_info_present_flag=0 -> this bit not present per spec.
    # initial_display_delay_present_flag=0 so skip those too.

    # frame_width_bits_minus_1(4) and frame_height_bits_minus_1(4)
    # choose 16 bits to carry sizes up to 65535
    fw_bits_minus1 = 15
    fh_bits_minus1 = 15
    bw.write_bits(fw_bits_minus1, 4)
    bw.write_bits(fh_bits_minus1, 4)

    max_w = rng.randrange(320, 1921)

    bw.write_bit(0)

    # use_128x128_superblock(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # enable_filter_intra(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # enable_intra_edge_filter(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)

    # enable_interintra_compound(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # enable_masked_compound(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # enable_warped_motion(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # enable_dual_filter(1)
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # enable_order_hint(1)
    enable_order_hint = 0
    bw.write_bit(enable_order_hint)
    if enable_order_hint:

        bw.write_bits(2, 3)
        bw.write_bit(0)  # enable_jnt_comp
        bw.write_bit(0)  # enable_ref_frame_mvs
    else:

    bw.write_bit(0)

    bw.write_bit(1)  # CDEF often present; set 1 or 0 both valid

    bw.write_bit(0)

# Build a single OBU block with header (has size field) and payload, then wrap with low-overhead length prefix

def build_obu(obu_type: int, payload: bytes, extension_flag: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # obu_header bits
    forbidden = 0
    obu_has_size_field = 1
    obu_reserved_1bit = 0
    header_bits = (forbidden << 7) | ((obu_type & 0x0F) << 3) | ((extension_flag & 1) << 2) | ((obu_has_size_field & 1) << 1) | (obu_reserved_1bit & 1)
    obu_header = bytes([header_bits])
    obu_size_field = leb128_encode_u(len(payload))
    obu = obu_header + obu_size_field + payload
    # Low overhead sample: prefix the whole OBU with outer length
    return leb128_encode_u(len(obu)) + obu

def build_temporal_delimiter() -> bytes:
    # temporal_delimiter has empty payload
    return build_obu(2, b"")

    stream = bytearray()

    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        stream += build_temporal_delimiter()
    stream += seq_header_obu

    # Keep size under 4096
    return bytes(stream)

    out.append(buffer_delay_len_minus1 & 0xFF)

    out.extend(struct.pack('<I', max_w_minus1))
    out.extend(struct.pack('<I', max_h_minus1))

    # bytes (uint16) length of following payload, then payload bytes
    out.extend(struct.pack('<H', len(payload)))

def _start_code(code: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([0x00, 0x00, 0x01, code & 0xFF])

def _u(nbits: int, value: int) -> List[int]:
    # Append bits (MSB-first within bytes). Collect bits as 0/1 list.
    return [((value >> (nbits - 1 - i)) & 1) for i in range(nbits)]

    out = bytearray()
    accum = 0
    cnt = 0
    for b in bits:
        accum = (accum << 1) | (b & 1)
        cnt += 1
        if cnt == 8:

            accum = 0
            cnt = 0

    # width(16), height(16), frame_rate_code(4), aspect_ratio_code(4)
    bits += _u(8, profile_idc)

            zero_count = 0
        out.append(b)

    return bytes(out)

    audiodatarate = rng.choice([64.0, 96.0, 128.0, 192.0, 256.0])
    videodatarate = rng.choice([500.0, 1000.0, 2500.0, 5000.0])
    stereo = rng.choice([True, False])

    # Build property entries
    entries = [
        ("width", float(width)),
        ("height", float(height)),
        ("framerate", float(framerate)),
        ("duration", float(duration)),
        ("videocodecid", float(videocodecid)),
        ("audiocodecid", float(audiocodecid)),
        ("audiodatarate", float(audiodatarate)),
        ("videodatarate", float(videodatarate)),
    ]

    # Write ECMA Array header
    out += _amf0_marker_ecma_array()
    out += _amf0_u32(len(entries) + 1)  # include stereo as boolean below
    # Write number properties
    for k, v in entries:
        out += _amf0_number(k, v)
    # Boolean property
    out += _amf0_u16(len("stereo")) + b"stereo" + _amf0_marker_boolean() + (b"\x01" if stereo else b"\x00")
    # End of object
    out += _amf0_marker_object_end()
    return bytes(out[:_MAX_BYTES])

# ---------------- Audio helpers (AAC) ----------------

def _aac_audio_specific_config(sample_rate: int, channels: int, profile_aot: int = 2) -> bytes:
    # Build MPEG-4 AudioSpecificConfig (GA) per ISO/IEC 14496-3
    # audioObjectType (5), samplingFrequencyIndex (4 or escape + 24), channelConfiguration (4)
    freq_table = [96000,88200,64000,48000,44100,32000,24000,22050,16000,12000,11025,8000,7350]
    if sample_rate in freq_table:
        sfi = freq_table.index(sample_rate)
        explicit = False
    else:
        sfi = 15
        explicit = True
    aot = profile_aot  # 2 = AAC LC
    # Pack first 5+4+4 bits
    bits = (aot & 0x1F) << (4 + 4)
    bits |= (sfi & 0x0F) << 4
    bits |= (channels & 0x0F)
    b0 = (bits >> 8) & 0xFF
    b1 = bits & 0xFF
    asc = bytearray([b0, b1])
    if explicit:
        asc += struct.pack('>I', sample_rate)[1:]  # 24-bit explicit frequency
    return bytes(asc)


def _aac_adts_frame(sample_rate: int, channels: int, payload_bytes: int, profile: int = 1) -> bytes:
    # Generate a minimal ADTS header (no CRC) + fake AAC payload of zeros
    # profile: 0: Main, 1: LC, 2: SSR -> store as (profile)
    freq_table = [96000,88200,64000,48000,44100,32000,24000,22050,16000,12000,11025,8000,7350]
    sfi = freq_table.index(sample_rate) if sample_rate in freq_table else 4  # default 44100
    chan = max(1, min(channels, 7))
    aac_frame_len = 7 + payload_bytes
    b = bytearray(7)
    # Syncword 0xFFF, MPEG-4, layer 00, protection_absent 1
    b[0] = 0xFF
    b[1] = 0xF1
    # profile(2), sampling_frequency_index(4), private(1), channel_config high 1
    b[2] = ((profile & 0x03) + 1) << 6
    b[2] |= (sfi & 0x0F) << 2
    b[2] |= (0 << 1)
    b[2] |= (chan >> 2) & 0x01
    # channel_config low 2, originality/home/copyright bits 0, frame length high 2
    b[3] = ((chan & 0x03) << 6) | ((aac_frame_len >> 11) & 0x03)
    # frame length middle 8
    b[4] = (aac_frame_len >> 3) & 0xFF
    # frame length low 3, buffer fullness 0x7FF high 5
    b[5] = ((aac_frame_len & 0x07) << 5) | 0x1F
    # buffer fullness low 6, number_of_raw_data_blocks_in_frame(2)=0
    b[6] = 0xFC
    return bytes(b) + (b"\x00" * payload_bytes)


def _build_audio_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # FLV Audio: 1 byte AudioTagHeader + optional AACPacketType + data
    # Choose AAC LC stereo 44.1/48k
    sample_rate = rng.choice([44100, 48000])
    channels = rng.choice([1, 2])
    # SoundFormat(4)=10(AAC), SoundRate(2)=3(44k) or 3 also used for 48k in FLV signaling, SoundSize(1)=1, SoundType(1)=stereo?
    sound_rate_code = 3  # 44kHz code; tolerated for AAC where rate is in payload
    sound_size = 1
    sound_type = 1 if channels == 2 else 0
    audio_hdr = ((10 & 0x0F) << 4) | ((sound_rate_code & 0x03) << 2) | ((sound_size & 0x01) << 1) | (sound_type & 0x01)

    aac_packet_type = rng.choice([0, 1])
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(audio_hdr)
    out.append(aac_packet_type)

    if aac_packet_type == 0:
        # Sequence header: AAC AudioSpecificConfig
        asc = _aac_audio_specific_config(sample_rate, channels, profile_aot=2)
        out += asc
    else:
        # Raw AAC frame (commonly ADTS not included by FLV, but many demuxers accept raw too).
        # We include a small valid ADTS frame to be robust.
        payload = _aac_adts_frame(sample_rate, channels, payload_bytes=rng.randint(16, 64), profile=1)
        out += payload

    return bytes(out[:_MAX_BYTES])

# ---------------- Video helpers (AVC/H.264) ----------------

def _avc_sps_pps() -> List[bytes]:
    # Minimal plausible SPS/PPS RBSPs for baseline profile 640x360-ish (not fully parsed by writer typically)
    # Use very small, syntactically acceptable NALs used commonly in tests.
    # NAL header byte is not stored inside avcC SPS/PPS, so we provide raw RBSP payloads here.
    sps = bytes([0x67, 0x42, 0x80, 0x1e, 0xd9, 0x01, 0x40, 0x7b, 0x20])
    pps = bytes([0x68, 0xce, 0x38, 0x80])
    return [sps, pps]


def _avc_decoder_configuration_record(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build AVCDecoderConfigurationRecord (ISO/IEC 14496-15)
    # configurationVersion(1)=1
    # AVCProfileIndication(1), profile_compatibility(1), AVCLevelIndication(1)
    # lengthSizeMinusOne(6bits of 0xFC | 2bits)
    # numOfSPS(5bits)
    # for each SPS: 2 bytes length + data
    # numOfPPS(1)
    # for each PPS: 2 bytes length + data
    sps, pps = _avc_sps_pps()
    profile = sps[1]  # rough pick from SPS
    compat = sps[2]
    level = sps[3]
    nalu_len_size_minus1 = rng.choice([0, 1, 3])  # prefer 1 or 3; 3 => 4-byte lengths

    rec = bytearray()
    rec += b"\x01"
    rec.append(profile)
    rec.append(compat)
    rec.append(level)
    rec.append(0xFC | (nalu_len_size_minus1 & 0x03))
    rec.append(0xE0 | 1)  # numOfSPS = 1
    rec += struct.pack('>H', len(sps))
    rec += sps
    rec.append(1)  # numOfPPS = 1
    rec += struct.pack('>H', len(pps))
    rec += pps
    return bytes(rec)


def _mp4_sample_from_nalus(nalus: List[bytes], nalu_len_size: int = 4) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for n in nalus:
        out += len(n).to_bytes(nalu_len_size, 'big')
        out += n
    return bytes(out)


def _build_video_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # FLV Video: 1 byte VideoTagHeader + AVCPacketType + 3-byte CTS + data
    # FrameType(4): 1 keyframe, 2 inter; CodecID(4)=7 AVC
    frame_type = rng.choice([1, 2])
    video_hdr = ((frame_type & 0x0F) << 4) | 7
    avc_packet_type = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])  # 0: sequence header, 1: NALUs, 2: EOS
    cts = rng.randint(-90000, 90000)

    out = bytearray()
    out.append(video_hdr)
    out.append(avc_packet_type)
    # 24-bit signed CTS
    cts24 = cts & 0xFFFFFF
    out.append((cts24 >> 16) & 0xFF)
    out.append((cts24 >> 8) & 0xFF)
    out.append(cts24 & 0xFF)

    if avc_packet_type == 0:
        # AVCDecoderConfigurationRecord
        out += _avc_decoder_configuration_record(rng)
    elif avc_packet_type == 1:
        # Length-prefixed sample with IDR + non-IDR NALs
        idr = b"\x65" + b"\x88" * rng.randint(20, 60)  # IDR NAL (type 5)
        non_idr = b"\x41" + b"\x77" * rng.randint(10, 30)  # non-IDR (type 1)
        # Prefix with SPS/PPS too to be generous
        sps, pps = _avc_sps_pps()
        sps_nal = b"\x67" + sps[1:]  # ensure nal header present; our sps already includes 0x67
        pps_nal = b"\x68" + pps[1:]
        sample = _mp4_sample_from_nalus([sps_nal, pps_nal, idr, non_idr], nalu_len_size=4)
        out += sample
    else:
        # End of sequence: no extra bytes needed
        pass

    return bytes(out[:_MAX_BYTES])

# ---------------- Entry point ----------------

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    choice = rng.choice(["audio", "video", "script"])  # stubs pick type independently, but we emit valid payloads
    if choice == "audio":
        buf = _build_audio_payload(rng)
    elif choice == "video":
        buf = _build_video_payload(rng)
    else:
        buf = _build_script_payload(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty and within limit
    if not buf:
        buf = b"\x02\x00\x00"  # minimal invalid-but-nonempty fallback, should not happen
    return buf[:_MAX_BYTES]

import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generate a variety of valid FLV headers. flv_header_read expects at least
# the 9-byte header. Providing extra bytes is fine; the fuzzer passes the
# whole buffer as input.
# FLV header format (big-endian fields on wire):
# 0-2:  'F' 'L' 'V'
# 3:    version (usually 0x01)
# 4:    flags bitfield: bit2(audio), bit0(video) in Adobe docs, but many libs use bit2 audio, bit0 video
# 5-8:  data offset (u32 BE), usually 9 for basic header, or >= 9 if extensions present
# Optionally followed by PreviousTagSize0 (4 bytes, value 0)
# We will craft many combinations covering:
# - different version values (1 and edge/odd values)
# - presence/absence of audio/video flags
# - data offset values: 9, >9, large, boundary
# - inclusion of PreviousTagSize after header
# - optional padding/junk bytes after to simulate real files

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096


def _u32be(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _pick_flags(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Typical: bit2 (0x04) audio, bit0 (0x01) video in many implementations
    choices = [0x00, 0x01, 0x04, 0x05]
    # Add some unusual but valid bits to see codepaths (reserved bits ignored by some parsers)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        choices.append(0xFF & rng.randrange(0, 256))
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _pick_version(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Common is 1; include edge variants to exercise tolerant readers
    choices = [1, 0, 2, 3, 0xFF]
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _build_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    version = _pick_version(rng)
    flags = _pick_flags(rng)

    # Choose a data offset
    # Must be >= 9 per spec; some files set larger when extension fields exist.
    offset_choices: List[int] = [9, 13, 15, 24]
    # Occasionally select a large but valid offset inside our buffer
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        offset_choices.append(rng.randint(9, 256))
    data_offset = rng.choice(offset_choices)

    hdr = b"FLV" + bytes([version, flags]) + _u32be(data_offset)

    # Optionally append PreviousTagSize0 (4 bytes of zero) immediately after header
    tail = b""
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        tail += _u32be(0)

    # If data_offset > 9, fill the gap between 9 and data_offset with zero padding or random bytes
    gap = max(0, data_offset - 9)
    if gap > 0:
        # We've already potentially appended 4 bytes of PreviousTagSize at header+9.
        # Ensure total bytes at least data_offset by adding gap padding if needed.
        # Decide content for padding region: zeros or pattern
        pad_len = max(0, gap - (4 if len(tail) >= 4 else 0))
        if pad_len > 0:
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                tail += b"\x00" * pad_len
            else:
                # Random-but-stable pattern bytes (not too large)
                tail += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(pad_len))

    # Optionally add a small, well-formed first tag header after data offset region to keep buffer realistic
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # PreviousTagSize0 again (legal between tags), then a minimal Script/Data tag header (type 18)
        tail += _u32be(0)
        # FLV tag header: [Type(1)][DataSize(3)][Timestamp(3)][TimestampExt(1)][StreamID(3)]
        tag_type = 18  # script tag
        data_size = rng.randrange(0, 32)  # small payload
        timestamp = rng.randrange(0, 1000)
        stream_id = 0
        tag_hdr = bytes([
            tag_type,
            (data_size >> 16) & 0xFF,
            (data_size >> 8) & 0xFF,
            data_size & 0xFF,
            (timestamp >> 16) & 0xFF,
            (timestamp >> 8) & 0xFF,
            timestamp & 0xFF,
            (timestamp >> 24) & 0xFF,  # TimestampExt
            (stream_id >> 16) & 0xFF,
            (stream_id >> 8) & 0xFF,
            stream_id & 0xFF,
        ])
        tail += tag_hdr
        # Add dummy payload matching data_size so tag looks consistent
        if data_size > 0:
            tail += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(data_size))
        # PreviousTagSize for this tag: header(11)+payload
        tail += _u32be(11 + data_size)

    return hdr + tail


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many candidate headers to concatenate or choose among
    # For this fuzzer stub, it reads only one header from the start, so we just return one crafted header
    buf = _build_header(rng)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]

    return buf

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets multiple FLV-related stubs that read/write headers and tag headers,
# plus various codec configuration loaders. We will output a small, valid-looking FLV file
# beginning with a correct FLV header, a PreviousTagSize0, and a small script tag carrying
# AMF0 onMetaData with a few fields. This exercises:
# - flv_header_read (valid header)
# - flv_tag_header_read (valid tag header)
# - flv_audio_tag_header_read/flv_video_tag_header_read (not used for script tag, but parser paths still see type)
# - flv_data_tag_header_read (script tag)
# - flv_reader_read (if backed by file, but here we only provide raw buffers; nonetheless many stubs accept arbitrary buffers)
# The AMF0 payload is simple and valid: [String "onMetaData"][ECMA array with 3 entries][Object End]
# Sizes are consistent and stay well under 4096 bytes.

# Helper: write big-endian 24-bit value

def be24(v: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([(v >> 16) & 0xFF, (v >> 8) & 0xFF, v & 0xFF])

# Helper: AMF0 encoders for common types used in onMetaData
AMF0_NUMBER = 0x00
AMF0_BOOLEAN = 0x01
AMF0_STRING = 0x02
AMF0_OBJECT = 0x03
AMF0_NULL = 0x05
AMF0_UNDEFINED = 0x06
AMF0_ECMA_ARRAY = 0x08
AMF0_OBJECT_END = b"\x00\x00\x09"


def amf0_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) <= 0xFFFF:
        return bytes([AMF0_STRING]) + struct.pack('>H', len(b)) + b
    # long string fallback
    return b"\x0C" + struct.pack('>I', len(b)) + b


def amf0_name(name: str) -> bytes:
    b = name.encode('utf-8')
    return struct.pack('>H', len(b)) + b


def amf0_number(val: float) -> bytes:
    return bytes([AMF0_NUMBER]) + struct.pack('>d', float(val))


def amf0_boolean(val: bool) -> bytes:
    return bytes([AMF0_BOOLEAN, 1 if val else 0])


def amf0_ecma_array(entries: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # ECMA array marker + associative count (we provide len(entries)) + entries + object end marker
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(AMF0_ECMA_ARRAY)
    out += struct.pack('>I', len(entries))
    for e in entries:
        out += e
    out += AMF0_OBJECT_END
    return bytes(out)


def build_onmetadata(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # onMetaData name as a string (preceded by AMF0 String marker)
    out = bytearray()
    out += amf0_string("onMetaData")

    # Build ECMA array with a few entries: duration (Number), width (Number), height (Number),
    # audiocodecid (Number), videocodecid (Number), canSeekToEnd (Boolean)
    duration = rng.uniform(0.0, 300.0)
    width = rng.choice([640, 854, 960, 1280, 1920])
    height = rng.choice([360, 480, 540, 720, 1080])
    audiocodecid = rng.choice([10, 2])  # AAC(10) or MP3(2)
    videocodecid = rng.choice([7, 12, 13])  # AVC(7), HEVC(12), AV1(13) typical FLV mappings
    can_seek = rng.choice([True, False])

    entries = []
    entries.append(amf0_name("duration") + amf0_number(duration))
    entries.append(amf0_name("width") + amf0_number(width))
    entries.append(amf0_name("height") + amf0_number(height))
    entries.append(amf0_name("audiocodecid") + amf0_number(audiocodecid))
    entries.append(amf0_name("videocodecid") + amf0_number(videocodecid))
    entries.append(amf0_name("canSeekToEnd") + amf0_boolean(can_seek))

    out += amf0_ecma_array(entries)
    return bytes(out)


def build_flv_header(has_audio: int, has_video: int, data_offset: int = 9) -> bytes:
    # Signature 'FLV', version 1, flags: audio bit (0x04), video bit (0x01)
    flags = (0x04 if has_audio else 0) | (0x01 if has_video else 0)
    header = bytearray()
    header += b"FLV"
    header += bytes([1, flags])
    header += struct.pack('>I', data_offset)
    return bytes(header)


def build_script_tag(payload: bytes, timestamp: int) -> bytes:
    # FLV tag header for script data (type=18), filter=0, data size=payload size, timestamp, streamId=0
    tag = bytearray()
    tag_type = 18
    data_size = len(payload)
    # Tag header: [Type(1)] [DataSize(3)] [Timestamp(3)] [TimestampExtended(1)] [StreamID(3)]
    tag += bytes([tag_type])
    tag += be24(data_size)
    ts = timestamp & 0xFFFFFFFF
    tag += be24(ts & 0xFFFFFF)
    tag += bytes([(ts >> 24) & 0xFF])
    tag += b"\x00\x00\x00"  # streamID
    return bytes(tag) + payload


def previous_tag_size(tag_with_header_and_body: bytes) -> bytes:
    # PreviousTagSize includes the size of tag header (11) + data size
    size = len(tag_with_header_and_body)
    return struct.pack('>I', size)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Randomly decide presence flags
    has_audio = rng.randint(0, 1)
    has_video = rng.randint(0, 1)

    header = build_flv_header(has_audio, has_video, 9)
    # PreviousTagSize0 (0) after header per FLV spec
    prev0 = struct.pack('>I', 0)

    # Build a small valid onMetaData script tag
    amf_payload = build_onmetadata(rng)
    # For data tags, payload should start with AMF type/value pairs already built
    script_tag = build_script_tag(amf_payload, timestamp=rng.randint(0, 5000))
    prev_script = previous_tag_size(script_tag)

    blob = header + prev0 + script_tag + prev_script

    # Keep size under 4096; optionally append another small script tag variant to add variety
    if len(blob) < 2048:
        # Add a second script tag with a different subset of fields to exercise counts and sizes
        amf2 = amf0_string("onMetaData") + amf0_ecma_array([
            amf0_name("stereo") + amf0_boolean(rng.choice([True, False])),
            amf0_name("framerate") + amf0_number(rng.choice([24.0, 25.0, 29.97, 30.0, 60.0])),
        ])
        script2 = build_script_tag(amf2, timestamp=rng.randint(0, 8000))
        prev2 = previous_tag_size(script2)
        blob += script2 + prev2

    # Ensure final size <= 4096
    return blob[:4096]

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# AAC ADTS utilities
# We will build one or more ADTS frames with plausible headers and small payloads.
# Keep total size <= 4096.

ADTS_SYNC = 0xFFF

AOT_AAC_LC = 2  # profile index in ADTS header (0: Main, 1: LC, 2: SSR) but ADTS stores (profile-1)
# Standard sampling frequency index table per MPEG-4 AAC
AAC_SFI_TABLE = [
    96000, 88200, 64000, 48000, 44100, 32000,
    24000, 22050, 16000, 12000, 11025, 8000, 7350,
]

# Choose a set of common configurations to improve validity
COMMON_CONFIGS: List[Tuple[int, int, int]] = [
    # (sampling_frequency_index, channel_configuration, profile)
    (3, 2, 2),   # 48kHz, stereo, LC
    (4, 2, 2),   # 44.1kHz, stereo, LC
    (5, 2, 2),   # 32kHz, stereo, LC
    (6, 1, 2),   # 24kHz, mono, LC
    (7, 2, 2),   # 22.05kHz, stereo, LC
    (8, 1, 2),   # 16kHz, mono, LC
]


def _make_adts_header(profile: int, sfi: int, chan_cfg: int, payload_len: int, 
                       mpeg_id: int = 0, protection_absent: int = 1,
                       private_bit: int = 0, home: int = 0,
                       original_copy: int = 0, copyright_ident: int = 0,
                       adts_buffer_fullness: int = 0x7FF, num_raw_blocks: int = 0) -> bytes:
    """
    Build a 7-byte ADTS header (without CRC) for a single AAC raw_data_block.
    profile is MPEG-4 Audio Object Type value (e.g., 2 for AAC LC). ADTS stores (profile-1) in header.
    sfi: sampling frequency index (0..12 common).
    chan_cfg: channel configuration (1..7 typical).
    payload_len: bytes of raw AAC frame following the header.
    mpeg_id: 0 for MPEG-4, 1 for MPEG-2 in ADTS layer.
    protection_absent: 1 -> no CRC (7-byte header). 0 -> CRC present (not used here).
    num_raw_blocks: number_of_raw_data_blocks_in_frame (0 => 1 block per frame).
    """
    # Frame length includes header (7) + payload
    aac_frame_length = 7 + payload_len
    if aac_frame_length > 0x1FFF:
        aac_frame_length = 0x1FFF  # clamp defensively

    # Pack fields per ISO/IEC 13818-7 ADTS fixed + variable headers
    # Fixed header (28 bits after 12-bit sync):
    # ID(1), layer(2=00), protection_absent(1), profile(2), sampling_frequency_index(4),
    # private_bit(1), channel_configuration(3), original_copy(1), home(1)
    # Variable header:
    # copyright_identification_bit(1), copyright_identification_start(1),
    # aac_frame_length(13), adts_buffer_fullness(11), number_of_raw_data_blocks_in_frame(2)

    syncword = ADTS_SYNC  # 12 bits of 1
    layer = 0
    prof_bits = max(0, profile - 1) & 0x3
    sfi_bits = sfi & 0xF
    chan_bits = chan_cfg & 0x7
    aac_frame_length &= 0x1FFF
    adts_buffer_fullness &= 0x7FF
    num_raw_blocks &= 0x3

    # Build 56 bits header (7 bytes)
    bits = 0
    bits |= (syncword & 0xFFF) << 44
    bits |= (mpeg_id & 0x1) << 43
    bits |= (layer & 0x3) << 41
    bits |= (protection_absent & 0x1) << 40
    bits |= (prof_bits & 0x3) << 38
    bits |= (sfi_bits & 0xF) << 34
    bits |= (private_bit & 0x1) << 33
    bits |= (chan_bits & 0x7) << 30
    bits |= (original_copy & 0x1) << 29
    bits |= (home & 0x1) << 28

    bits |= (copyright_ident & 0x1) << 27  # copyright_identification_bit
    bits |= (0 & 0x1) << 26                 # copyright_identification_start
    bits |= (aac_frame_length & 0x1FFF) << 13
    bits |= (adts_buffer_fullness & 0x7FF) << 2
    bits |= (num_raw_blocks & 0x3)

    hdr = bits.to_bytes(7, byteorder='big')
    return hdr


def _gen_aac_raw_frame(rng: random.Random, sf_index: int, channels: int) -> bytes:

    so return structured-but-random bytes with constraints to keep decoders tolerant.

    # Choose payload size in a typical range for LC: ~12 to ~200 bytes

    payload = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
    if size >= 2 and payload[0] == 0xFF:
        payload[0] ^= 0x55
    return bytes(payload)


def _build_adts_frames(rng: random.Random, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:

        chan_cfg = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])
